text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every trace contained the same six activities between A30 and A31: A33, A35 and A36 ran in no fixed order among themselves, followed by A37, A38 and A39 in no fixed order; each cross-trio pair co-occurred in 99–100 in 100 traces, always with the first trio before the second [REL001, REL013, REL015, REL022, REL025].
- In the later window, A30 and A31 still appear in every trace, but the six middle activities each appear in only about 47 in 100 traces (A33, A35, A36) to about 56 in 100 traces (A37, A38, A39), still at most once per trace, whereas before each appeared in 100 in 100 [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006].
- The six now form two almost mutually exclusive trios: A33, A35 and A36 still occur together whenever any of them occurs (jointly in about 47 in 100 later-window traces, otherwise none of the three), and likewise A37, A38 and A39 (about 56 in 100); cross-trio pairs that previously shared a trace in 99–100 in 100 cases now do so in only about 3 in 100 [REL013, REL015, REL017, REL022, REL024, REL025].
- Ordering relative to the anchors is preserved: whenever one of the six executes, A30 still comes before it and it still comes before A31, in essentially all of their joint appearances in both windows [POS001, POS002, REL001, REL006, REL007, REL012].
- Successor profiles shifted accordingly: A30's outgoing transitions, previously almost exclusively to A33, A35 and A36 (about 34, 36 and 28 in 100), are now spread roughly evenly over all six activities; A33, A35 and A36 now lead either to a trio member or directly to A31 (roughly a quarter to a third of their outgoing edges), where before they led on to the second trio [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004].
- Event-position distances shrank: A37, A38 and A39 now follow A30 after 1–3 positions (about 94 in 100 of observed pairs) instead of 4–5, and A31 now follows A33, A35 and A36 after 1–3 positions instead of 4–5, consistent with a middle block of three activities instead of six [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG006, LAG009].
- For context, 54 control-flow items qualified against fewer than 1 expected for an unchanged process, and every item's difference exceeds about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled data, so this volume cannot be explained by sampling noise alone [screening].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis of a structural change in the segment between A30 and A31: the six-activity block A33, A35, A36, A37, A38, A39, which in the earlier window executed in full in every trace, appears in the later window as two almost mutually exclusive alternatives — in roughly 47 in 100 traces only A33, A35 and A36 execute, in roughly 56 in 100 only A37, A38 and A39, and in about 3 in 100 both trios — so the block as a whole became optional (skipped in roughly half of the cases) while each trio remained all-or-nothing [OCC001, OCC004, REL015, REL025].

The signs are direct and consistent: participation of all six activities fell from 100% to about 47–57% while A30 and A31 stayed at 100%; within-trio co-occurrence was retained and cross-trio co-occurrence collapsed from 99–100 in 100 to about 3 in 100; the order A30 → executing activities → A31 is unchanged; and successor and distance profiles match the same picture. Limitations: the many items largely re-describe one underlying trace behaviour and are not independent confirmations, and the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows sample different case mixes that always followed these different paths, rather than a modification of one process; the near-exclusivity of the trios is also not absolute (about 3 in 100 later-window traces contain both) [REL017, REL027, OCC003, screening].

Other differences: minor positional shifts — A30's mean relative position moved slightly later (about 0.62 to 0.67 of the trace) and A31's slightly earlier (about 0.82 to 0.80), consistent with the shorter middle block; and the few items on cross-trio distances rest on only 4–5 later-window observations and should be treated as weak [POS001, POS002, LAG005, LAG007, LAG008, LAG010, LAG011].
